advisories.title: Internal gRPC API does not require authentication by default in distributed mode
advisories.summary:
### Summary

In a distributed deployment (`cluster.enabled: true`), Qdrant peers communicate over an internal gRPC API, port 6335 by default. Before v1.20.0 this port did not require authentication unless the operator enabled `service.enforce_internal_auth` (available since v1.18.0, off by default). The internal listener binds to the same address as the public API (`service.host`), so the port is reachable wherever the public API is reachable, unless the network prevents it.

### Impact

A host with network access to port 6335, without an API key and without being a member of the cluster, can:

- call `AddPeerToKnown` and add a peer of its choice to the cluster; a cluster member receives replicated shards, giving read access to stored data;
- send Raft messages that the consensus state machine processes without a sender check, allowing modification of cluster state (collections, shard placement, peer topology);
- send messages of unbounded size to the internal services and exhaust memory on the node.

Single-node deployments do not start the internal port.

### Patches

From v1.20.0, `service.enforce_internal_auth` defaults to enabled. With it enabled, the internal API accepts only `api_key` and `alt_api_key`. Enforcement requires an API key to be configured; a distributed deployment with no API key remains unauthenticated on the internal port and, since v1.19.2, logs a warning at startup.

v1.20.0 does not introduce a message-size limit on the internal port. With enforcement enabled, reaching the internal port requires the admin API key.

Rolling upgrades to v1.20.0 follow the usual one-minor-version rule. Peers on v1.19.x already attach the API key to internal requests, so mixed 1.19/1.20 clusters keep working during the upgrade.

### Workarounds

For versions before v1.20.0:

1. Restrict port 6335 to the nodes of the same cluster with a firewall, security group or NetworkPolicy. Not merely "not reachable from the internet": if your application tier can reach 6333, check that it cannot reach 6335.
2. On v1.18.0 or later: set the same `api_key` on every peer, then set `service.enforce_internal_auth: true` and restart one peer at a time. Enable TLS for internal communication (`cluster.p2p.enable_tls: true`) so the key is not sent in plain text.
3. From v1.19.2: set `cluster.p2p.host` to an internal IP address so the internal port is not bound to the interface serving the public API. The node's peer URI (`--uri`) must point to the same address.

See [Enforce Authentication on Internal Communication](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/security/#enforce-authentication-on-internal-communication).

### Qdrant Cloud

Managed Cloud clusters run with a NetworkPolicy, enforced by Calico, that allows ingress on port 6335 only from pods of the same cluster; customer traffic gateways cannot reach the port. Managed Cloud is not materially affected. Hybrid Cloud and Private Cloud: the operator provisions the same policy; enforcement depends on the customer's CNI.

### Related

GHSA-3gph-6c29-p29v: with `enforce_internal_auth` enabled, versions before v1.19.2 also accepted the read-only API key and JWTs on the internal API.

### Credits

Reported by Davi Ottenheimer (Ottenheimer GmbH) on 9 July 2026; received by Qdrant via CERT-Bund (BSI) on 21 September 2026, and independently by @zerovulnlabs via GitHub private vulnerability reporting.

### References

- qdrant/qdrant#10854 (default change)
- qdrant/qdrant#10852, #10853
- https://qdrant.tech/documentation/security/

advisories.title: Read-only API key and JWTs accepted on internal gRPC API when enforce_internal_auth is enabled
advisories.summary:
### Summary

In a distributed deployment, Qdrant peers communicate over an internal gRPC API (port 6335 by default). Since v1.18.0, `service.enforce_internal_auth` requires authentication on this port. When enabled, the internal API accepted the same credentials as the public API, including the read-only API key and JWTs. The internal services do not check per-request access, so a caller holding only a read-only credential could add a peer to the cluster and perform write operations such as creating payload indexes.

### Impact

With `enforce_internal_auth: true`, a holder of the read-only API key or of any JWT, with network access to port 6335, could:

- call `AddPeerToKnown` and add a peer of their choice to the cluster;
- call internal write operations, for example `CreateFieldIndex`.

### Patches

Fixed in v1.19.2. The internal gRPC API now accepts only `api_key` and `alt_api_key`. The read-only key and all JWTs, including those with manage access, are rejected with `Unauthenticated`.

### Default configuration

Deployments that do not enable `enforce_internal_auth` are not affected by this issue.

### Qdrant Cloud

Managed Cloud clusters run with a NetworkPolicy, enforced by Calico, that allows ingress on port 6335 only from pods of the same cluster. The gateways carrying customer traffic cannot reach port 6335. Managed Cloud is not materially affected.

Hybrid Cloud and Private Cloud: the Qdrant operator provisions the same NetworkPolicy. Enforcement depends on the CNI of the customer's Kubernetes cluster.

### References

- [Security documentation: Enforce Authentication on Internal Communication](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/security/#enforce-authentication-on-internal-communication)
- qdrant/qdrant#10758

advisories.title: Qdrant affected by arbitrary file write via `/logger` endpoint
advisories.summary: Qdrant is a vector similarity search engine and vector database. From 1.9.3 to before 1.16.0, it is possible to append to arbitrary files via /logger endpoint using an attacker-controlled on_disk.log_file path. Minimal privileges are required (read-only access). This vulnerability is fixed in 1.16.0.
